In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the genetic factors that contribute to cancer development.
the development of a new approach for the diagnosis and prognosis of cancer in general and breast cancer in particular.

the development and implementation of new technologies in the field of molecular diagnostics, and the development of innovative diagnostic methods for the detection of genetic disorders and infectious diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a young patient with ovarian cancer and a positive family history should be referred for genetic testing.
the family history is of utmost importance to determine the prior probability of finding a mutation in women 35 years or younger with ovarian cancer.
the risk of finding a mutation is higher in women 40 or younger if they have a first-degree relative affected with ovarian cancer or breast cancer, and if they have a family history of both cancers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of a first-degree relative with breast and/or epithelial ovarian cancer in a young woman is an independent predictor for the presence of a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation.
family history can be used to predict risk of BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations in women under 40 with ovarian cancer, and this information can be helpful for genetic counselors and oncologists.
the risk of finding a pathogenic variant in a woman with epithelial ovarian carcinoma is not determined by the age at which the diagnosis is made but rather by the family history of the patient.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the risk of BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation in early-onset epithelia ovarian cancer is similar to that in all ages of ovarian cancer, and family history is the main determinant for referral for genetic testing.
family history is the main determinant in deciding whether or not to test for BRCA mutations in women with epithelial ovarian cancers.
family history is an important determinant in the risk of BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutation.
